A Significant Ruling on Blacklisting, Civil Consequences & Tender Eligibility | Patna High Court
Privileged to have had the opportunity to assist Adv. Avanish Kumar Singh Rana Sir, before the Hon’ble Patna High Court, in a matter concerning the legal consequences of an order of blacklisting which had subsequently been recalled by the competent authority.
The Hon’ble Division Bench comprising Hon’ble Mr. Justice Sudhir Singh and Hon’ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Kumar Verma considered an important question arising in the context of administrative action and public procurement.
The Hon’ble Court observed that blacklisting is a serious administrative action having civil consequences, as it directly affects the commercial reputation and future prospects of a contractor.
Importantly, where the competent authority itself subsequently recalls an order of blacklisting and restores the contractor’s eligibility, the adverse consequences of the intervening period cannot be permitted to continue as an adverse antecedent.
The Court accordingly directed that the period during which the petitioner remained blacklisted, from 20.03.2024 to 05.09.2024, shall stand expunged for all practical purposes and shall not be treated as a disqualification or adverse antecedent in any future tender or contractual process.
The judgment reinforces an important principle of fairness, proportionality and administrative justice: once an adverse administrative action has been consciously recalled, its residual stigma cannot ordinarily be allowed to continue to prejudice the affected party.
Grateful for the opportunity to assist in a matter involving significant principles of Administrative Law, Blacklisting, Natural Justice, Proportionality and Public Procurement Law.
The order is annexed for reference.
